essence: Grace first discloses the world as His, without remainder, now — then identity is declared outright: Maheśa, always my self, and all mine through Him.
Appearance, then ownership: grace showing the world as His before identity claims it.
The non-dual recognition (pratyabhijñā) is here performed as a two-step: disclosure, then declaration.

sections.SUMMARY: Grace first discloses the world as His; then identity declared outright: Maheśa, always my self — and all mine through Him.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at grace disclosing the world as His. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual identity, not the joy of acquisition — all is mine already, through Him.
